For `kotlin-logging-extensions/`: a Kotlin Symbol Processing (KSP) plugin generating kotlin-logging `log` extensions. Prioritize correctness, generated-code safety, developer ergonomics, deterministic and explicit behavior, and compatibility across documented Kotlin/KSP/kotlin-logging versions.

`processor`: KSP logic, code generation, processor tests. `workload`: consumer examples and integration/regression tests. `scripts`: release and maintenance scripts. Preserve strict module boundaries between processor implementation and workload examples. Keep KSP processing logic in `processor`; do not move processor behavior into `workload`. Keep `workload` focused on usage scenarios and regression coverage for generated code behavior.

Keep generation rules stable and backward-compatible unless an intentional breaking change is requested. Preserve deterministic file naming and package handling in generated files. Do not introduce breaking changes to generated API shape without updating tests and compatibility documentation. Keep user-facing docs and compatibility guidance aligned with actual behavior. Prefer clear naming and predictable output over clever abstractions; design for readers with explicit behavior, constraints, and failure modes. Keep processor behavior explicit and test-proven. Avoid unnecessary symbol resolution and processing overhead in KSP flows. Add concise comments only when intent is not obvious from code.

Always use the Gradle wrapper: `./gradlew ...`.
full build: `./gradlew clean build`
